_role: The machine-readable record of what the autonomy loop may put in public without asking. Read by research/autonomy/publish_bar.py::authority_permits. It is NOT the grant — trimcrae is. This file only records his grant so a script can check it.
_read_this_when: You are about to post anything, or you are about to edit this file. Editing it is a DECLARED change (architecture §10.4): it goes in amendments.jsonl, and it may not be made by the cycle that this file just blocked.
_this_file_disagreeing_with_claude_md_is: CLAUDE.md §3 and AGENTS.md were amended in the same commit that first set standing_grant to true. If a future reader finds this file permitting what those forbid, THIS file is wrong and the post does not happen.

aixiv.granted_by: trimcrae, 2026-08-26, AskUserQuestion D1, verbatim: 'Broad: any paper meeting the bar'
granted_against: the bar is the six clauses in research/autonomy/publish_bar.py, every one computed from a committed artifact
aiXiv only — no other venue, ever
every journal submission still escalates immediately (decision D4)
aixiv._re_ask_if: ANY item in granted_against stops being true. The grant was given against that backdrop, not in general. Widening it is not an amendment the loop may make — it is a new grant, and only trimcrae issues one.

scope.papers: ANY publication endpoint passing all clauses, EXCEPT those in `excluded_papers`. Deliberately not an allow-list — see granted_by — but the deny-list is explicit and is checked before any post.
scope._max_versions_why: aixiv-submission §3, measured: ELEVEN versions of aixiv.260822.000005 never moved its rating above 6 and it trended DOWN as the paper improved. Iterating prose does not move the number, so an uncapped loop would rediscover that at trimcrae's expense and put ten near-identical versions under his ORCID. Three is enough for a real correction and too few for a rating chase.
scope._notify_why: Not a gate — he does not approve the post, he learns of it. Escalation trigger 1 covers journals; this covers aiXiv.

PUB-ASO.why: trimcrae, 2026-08-27, verbatim: 'That's the only paper that shouldn't auto ship to aiXiv.' PUB-ASO is posted on Qeios as a preprint with a DOI (10.32388/VL3LJR) and a version history he controls. Its versions are HIS act, on HIS venue; a second public home for the same paper, posted by the loop, would fragment the record under his ORCID and create two version histories for one work. ⛔ THIS IS A NARROWING OF THE STANDING GRANT, NOT A WIDENING — it removes a permission the loop had and adds none, so it is an amendment the loop may make. Re-widening it is NOT: that would be a new grant, and only trimcrae issues one.
PUB-ASO.applies_to_venue: aiXiv only. Qeios is unaffected and was never covered by this grant — every Qeios post remains trimcrae's own act, prepared by the loop and posted by him.

forbidden_regardless_of_the_bar: retitling or reframing a paper to clear a clause or chase a venue's taste — CLAUDE.md §3, the title is what a reader searches
posting a claim that exceeds its endpoint's recorded claim_ceiling — that is clause 3 and no grant overrides it
posting a review of our own paper to aiXiv, or any act that would place a fabricated review under trimcrae's name — aixiv-submission §0
treating an aiXiv Rating as evidence of anything

journal._constant: Not a parameter. No bar reaches it, no amendment may set it true. A journal submission costs money, is slow to undo, and picks an identifier someone may cite. It escalates to trimcrae immediately (D4) with the venue shortlist and its evidence.

everything_else._covers: Zenodo publication, a GitHub release, a DOI mint, email to a corresponding author, any outward-facing act not named above. Preparing them needs no permission; performing them does and was not granted.
